name: 2018 livery
description: White fuselage; behind the wing a teal sweep rises from the belly to the crown ahead of the fin, with a navy wedge at the fin root; 'WESTJET' in heavy navy italic capitals over the forward windows with a small Canadian flag by the door; the fin a faceted design of teal, white and navy (a stylised mountain and maple-leaf pattern, finely dotted); navy winglets.

sources.title: Wikipedia: WestJet
sources.note: The 2018 rebrand that came with the 787.

pale.name: the fin's light half-tone (teal dots on white), as one tone

areas.name: teal sweep: lower aft fuselage from the belly behind the wing up to the crown ahead of the fin, and the tail cone
navy wedge at the fin root
light half-tone field across the middle, with the white maple-leaf point rising into the teal
teal wedge at the leading edge over the white band
white band rising from the leading edge aft, then turning down to the root
navy at the root forward of the white

logos.description: A small Canadian flag over the windows just behind the forward door, 'Proudly' small above it.

titles.style: WestJet's wordmark: heavy, slanted, slab-like capitals in navy over the forward windows, the J dropping below the line.

notes: Drawn from right-side photos only (C-GPFT 2024, C-FNWD 2025) and mirrored: the left side should match. The fin's facets are simplified to two areas. WestJet Encore (WEN) wears this scheme. Re-checked 2026-11-15 on C-GPFT (flipped, fitted to the measured 737-800 shape, whose fuselage the MAX 8 shares): the title's baseline is just under the windows' middle (about 0.3 m below it, y 0.085) and its capitals stand about 0.77 m above it (height 0.40; it had been drawn reaching most of the way to the crown); x 0.16 to 0.37 as drawn. The teal's front edge is straight from the side: drawn by its two ends. The fin's facets stay simplified (the white is a dotted gradient on the aircraft). WestJet's 737-800s, its commonest type, wear the same layout. Fin redrawn 2026-11-26 on C-GPFT (right side, flipped and fitted to shapes/B38M.json, read in fin space) and checked on 787-9 C-GMKS's left side (2023-10-05): teal above and aft; a light half-tone field across the middle with a white point rising to x 0.4, y 0.82 (the maple leaf's tip); a white band rising from the leading edge (y 0.2-0.26) to the trailing edge (y 0.39), turning down to the root at x 0.69-0.79; navy forward of it at the root; a teal wedge at the leading edge. The half-tones are drawn as flat tones. The fin's tail-art logo entry is gone: the areas are the art, and a separate mark drew a second, simpler version over them.
history: Replaces Skyarium v1's approximate standard (a few colors from memory). The 2018 livery replaced WestJet's teal-and-blue 'tail' scheme of the 2000s.
